capabilities.title: Role capability table
capabilities.description: Each cell is the lowest role a service principal needs for that action on that resource — the role cap its grant in that project must reach. The whole table is generated from the same matrix the backend evaluates (ACTION_REQUIRED_ROLE), so the table and the engine cannot drift apart.
capabilities.group_workspace_note: Reads only — the engine rejects writes on these outright.
capabilities.legend_required_role: Cell value = minimum role required (the grant's role cap must be at least this).
capabilities.legend_not_registered: — means the action is unavailable: the engine refuses writes on workspace-level resources outright, and any resource/action pair it never registered is denied by default.
capabilities.legend_ownership: * marks cells the ownership rule will tighten once it lands.

rules.scope_grant: Inside a project three things must all hold: a scope row covers the action, the project has an active grant, and the grant's role cap reaches the minimum role in the table.
rules.owner_floor: On top of that, the principal's owner must be an active workspace member whose own workspace role reaches the role the action requires.
rules.guest: Guest: read only. It can never create, update or delete.
rules.member: Member: reads every project resource and creates the everyday ones (work items, comments, pages, cycles, modules, states, stickies, assets, labels).
rules.member_ownership: Member may only update or delete resources it created itself; other people's items stay read-and-comment only.
rules.admin: Admin: not limited by ownership — it can act on any resource, including deleting ones it did not create.
rules.unknown_owner: When ownership is unknown (records that predate creator tracking) the default is deny.
rules.coming_soon: The three ownership rules above are not enforced yet — they land together with per-resource ownership enforcement. Until then a Member role cap still allows update and delete on anything in the table; the cells marked * are the ones that will tighten.
rules.workspace_level: Project, member, user and invite are workspace-level: they can be read but never written, and their read scope has to be workspace-wide (all projects).
rules.read_covers_list: A read scope also satisfies list requests, which is why no separate list row appears anywhere.
rules.default_deny: Anything the table does not cover — including a resource/action pair the backend never registered — is denied by default.
rules.invite: Reading invites needs Member or above, stricter than the other workspace-level resources.

A workspace admin can grant any principal access to this project below — toggling on writes both the grant and the scope rows the engine requires, and toggling off removes the grant.
